title: Babur Submits and Seeks Guru Nanak's Favor

blocks.text: Babur now realizes that Guru Nanak already knows the intention he has not fully spoken aloud. That recognition breaks his earlier arrogance and convinces him that the Guru stands near the divine in a way no imperial calculation can master.
Using the courtly idiom of the account, Babur addresses Guru Nanak as a great pir and asks whether the hopes that brought him here can truly be fulfilled.

The political question returns, but in a changed tone. Babur no longer speaks as a challenger testing a saint; he speaks as a seeker who wants confirmation that the transfer of rule he has heard about lies within the Guru's knowledge and permission.
